Overview

Screen Mirroring lets people cast their phone, videos and apps to a smart TV. Mirroring itself is easy — connecting is where people get stuck. I redesigned onboarding, Home and every connection state so the TV link is always clear.

MY ROLE

Redesigned onboarding for two cases: with Wi-Fi and without it

Designed the new Home, built around the TV connection

Mapped every connection state, from searching to disconnect

Delivered 23 hi-fi screens, ready for development

The problem

Mirroring is easy. Connecting is the hard part.

Before anything appears on the TV, four things have to go right. When one fails, most casting apps just show an empty screen — and people give up.

Research

I looked at where people drop off before they ever mirror anything.

Competitor review

Store reviews

Flow audit

01

Connection status is invisible

People couldn’t tell if the TV was connected, so they tapped features that didn’t work yet.

02

Wi-Fi is the first blocker

Many sessions failed before search even started, because the phone wasn’t on Wi-Fi.

03

Empty search feels broken

When no TV was found, a blank list looked like the app had crashed.

Key decisions

01

Connection status pinned to the top

Why: Mirroring only works once the TV is connected, so connection is the first thing people see — not the features.

02

Guided states instead of errors

Why: ‘No TV found’ explains what to check and offers Search again; ‘No Wi-Fi’ offers Turn on Wi-Fi. There is always a next step.

03

Two onboarding paths

Why: Splitting by Wi-Fi means people with Wi-Fi never see a step they don’t need.

Testing

Before handover, I tested the prototype with colleagues at Terafort — and fixed what slowed them down.

10+

Terafort colleagues

3 roles

developers, QA, designer

4 tasks

connect · mirror · disconnect · no Wi-Fi

What testing changed

— Not sure if the TV was connected → status bar pinned to the top of Home, with ‘Connected’ in green

— An empty list when no TV was found felt like a bug → ‘No device found’ now explains what to check and offers Search again

— Nothing happened while connecting → a clear ‘Connecting…’ loader on the selected TV

Accessibility & privacy

Accessible by default

✓ 48dp touch targets on every action

✓ Contrast checked on blue cards (WCAG 2.1 AA)

✓ Status shown with text, not colour alone

Privacy (GDPR)

✓ Local network permission explained before asking

✓ Only device names shown in search

✓ Ads labelled clearly as ‘Ad’

Outcome

Shipped at Terafort · 2026

Live on Google Play with 10K+ downloads. That’s the reach of the whole app and team — not something I’d pin on the design alone.

What I’m tracking

01

Share of people who connect a TV in their first session

02

Drop-off on the ‘No TV found’ screen

03

Time from opening the app to first mirror

What I learned

01

Design the failure states first

‘No Wi-Fi’ and ‘No TV found’ shaped the whole flow more than the happy path.

02

Ads need room too

Planning ad slots early kept them from covering real controls.
